launch.description: Arguments of `launch` as the engine receives them. The extension resolves launch.json first: a `.dll` program becomes `program: <dotnet.exe of the chosen bitness>, args: [<dll>, ...]`, and a .NET Framework exe gets `__dotnetFramework`. launch.json properties that only the extension reads (`architecture`, `sourceFileMap`, `sourceSearchPaths`, `processName`, `waitTimeout`) are not listed here.

program.description: Full path of the exe to start (a .NET apphost, a .NET Framework exe, or dotnet.exe). Not needed with `dumpPath`.

dumpPath.description: Open this crash dump (.dmp with full memory) instead of starting a program (read only; capability `netdbgSupportsDumps`). The engine must have the bitness of the dumped process (the extension chooses it; a 32-bit process written as a 64-bit dump counts as x86). After `configurationDone` the engine sends `process` (without `systemProcessId`; `dumpProcessId` is the number in the dump) and `stopped` (`exception` on the thread that was throwing, else `pause`, with the description `Crash dump`). `continue`, the steps, `pause`, `goto`, `setVariable`, `setExpression`, `netdbg.applyChanges`, `netdbg.freezeThread`, `netdbg.makeObjectId`, `netdbg.processUsage` and expressions that run code are refused with the reason.

env.description: Environment variables added for the program. `null` removes a variable.

stopAtEntry.description: Stop at the first line of the user's `Main` (also for `async Main`).

justMyCode.description: Only modules with symbols, without `DebuggerNonUserCode` / `DebuggerHidden` / `DebuggerStepThrough`, are user code (default true).

enableStepFiltering.description: Step over property accessors and operators when stepping in (default true).

editAndContinue.description: Edit and Continue (default true): modules of a Debug build with symbols are loaded so that `netdbg.applyChanges` can update them. The extension sets it from `netdbg.editAndContinue.enabled` unless launch.json does.

decompile.description: Assemblies of the application without symbols are decompiled to C# by the engine (`app`, the default), or not (`off`). See `netdbg.decompile`.

sqlLog.description: SQL log: read the commands the program runs through ADO.NET at the provider, without stopping (`netdbg.sqlExecuted`). `methods` replaces the provider methods (`Namespace.Type.Method`). The extension sets it from `netdbg.sqlLog.*` unless launch.json does.

exceptionLog.description: Exception log: record every thrown exception, also those that do not stop the program (`netdbg.exceptionThrown`); `snapshot` takes the stack and locals at the throw (default true). The extension sets it from `netdbg.exceptionLog.*`.

uiFreeze.description: UI freeze watch (default on, 2000 ms): a UI thread that does not answer window messages for `thresholdMs` while the program runs pauses it there (`netdbg.uiFrozen`, then `stopped` with reason `pause`). The extension sets it from `netdbg.uiFreeze.*`.

coverage.description: Code coverage: count the lines and branches the program runs (`netdbg.coverageChanged`, `netdbg.coverage`); the Cobertura XML is written when the session ends, into `folder` (absolute) or `%LOCALAPPDATA%\netdbg\coverage`. The extension sets it from `netdbg.coverage.*` unless launch.json does.

childProcesses.description: Processes the program starts with `Process.Start`: `record` (default) logs them (`netdbg.childProcess`), `follow` also suspends a .NET child and sends the reverse request `startDebugging` (`attach` with `processId` and `__resumeChild`) so that the client debugs it in its own session, `off` ignores them.

__dotnetFramework.description: Set by the extension when `program` is a .NET Framework exe: the engine starts it with the .NET Framework CLR (no .NET runtime needed).

attach.description: Arguments of `attach`. The process must have its runtime (coreclr.dll or clr.dll) loaded and be of the engine's bitness.

processId.description: Process id. A string is accepted too (`${command:pickProcess}` returns one).

decompile.description: As in launch (the application's folder is the folder of the process's exe).

__resumeChild.description: Set by the parent's engine in its `startDebugging` request: the process is a child it suspended before its runtime started. The engine registers for the runtime's start and then resumes it (a .NET Framework child is resumed and attached once its runtime has loaded).

messages.name: netdbg.applyChanges
messages.description: Edit and Continue: applies the saved edits of the program's C# sources to the program, without restarting (launched, not attached; a Debug build). The engine has its helper (`encdelta`, run with the Roslyn of the installed .NET SDK 9+) build the change against the sources as they were when debugging started, applies it with `ApplyChanges`, and moves breakpoints to the new code. Changed methods run the new code from their next call; a method that is running moves to the new code at its next statement unless that statement's line was changed. A running program is paused for the moment it takes. Also sends `netdbg.changesApplied`, `output` and, when applied, `invalidated`.

files.description: The saved files (paths as the PDB has them; the relay maps them through `sourceFileMap`). Omitted: every source of the program.

status.description: `applied`, `noChanges`, `rude` (an edit that needs a restart), `errors` (compile errors) or `failed`.

applied.description: The modules changed and how many methods each.

problems.description: Where an edit cannot be applied, or a compile error (line and column from 1).

details.description: Further reasons, one per line (the helper could not start, the source changed before debugging, ...).

messages.name: netdbg.coverage
messages.description: Code coverage of the session (launch argument `coverage`): the rates, and with `file` the state of each line of that file (the editor colors them). With `write`, writes the Cobertura XML now (into `folder`, absolute, when given).

uncountableBranches.description: Branches whose outcome cannot be counted (e.g. a switch on a computed value).

lines.description: With `file`: each line that has code. A line that ran but did not take every branch outcome has branchesCovered < branchesValid.

messages.name: netdbg.decompile
messages.description: Decompiled sources of assemblies without symbols. The engine decompiles the application's assemblies that have no PDB (not .NET's own) itself, when they are first needed: a frame in them, a step into them, a breakpoint in a decompiled file, or this request. The C# files are written to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\netdbg\decompiled\<MVID>-v<version>` and the symbols are made in memory, so in the same session frames point at the files, breakpoints bind in them and locals have names. The engine then sends `module` (`changed`, `symbolStatus` `Symbols decompiled.`). Symbols found on disk or in `NETCOREDBG_SYMBOL_DIRS` (downloaded ones) take precedence. Methods it cannot turn into C# are shown as IL. Without `module`, lists the assemblies decompiled on demand. The MCP tool `decompile` sends this request.

module.description: File name (`MyApp.dll`) or full path of a loaded assembly. Omitted: list the assemblies decompiled on demand.

type.description: With module: a type (`Namespace.Type`, `Type`, `Outer.Inner` or `Outer+Inner`); returns the numbered lines of its file.

method.description: With type: a member name (method, constructor = the type's name, property, event); only its lines (all overloads).

modules.description: Without `module`: the assemblies decompiled on demand.

file.description: With `type`: the file of the type, the line ranges returned (from 1, inclusive), the lines, and whether `maxLines` cut them.

messages.name: netdbg.freezeThread
messages.description: Freezes or thaws a thread: a frozen thread stays suspended across `continue`, steps and evaluations until thawed.

threadId.description: The thread (`threads`' id, the OS thread id).

messages.name: netdbg.handleStats
messages.description: For the types that hold a native handle in a field, counts the objects and those whose handle is not 0 (not disposed). The field may be declared by a base type (`Bitmap` holds `Image._nativeImage`).

fields.description: The fields to look at, by declaring type (`Namespace.Name`) and field name.

types.description: By type name; types without one of the fields are left out.

messages.name: netdbg.heapStats
messages.description: Counts the objects on the GC heap by type, while the program is stopped. Fails while a GC is in progress.

types.description: Largest total size first. Free space between objects is counted under the name `?`.

messages.name: netdbg.makeObjectId
messages.description: Gives the object a value refers to an id (`$1`) that stays valid while the program runs (a weak GC handle: it does not keep the object alive, and reads `null` once the object is collected). In expressions the extension writes `$1` as `__NETDBG_OBJID_1`; values of objects with an id end with ` {$1}`.

id.description: The new id (1, 2, ...); the same object asked twice keeps its first id.

messages.name: netdbg.processUsage
messages.description: The program's process usage now, read by the engine from the process it debugs (running or stopped). The memory graph asks for it once a second.

cpuMs.description: CPU time (kernel + user) since the process started; the usage comes from the change between two readings.

gdiQuota.description: The per-process limits of GDI / USER objects (10,000 unless changed in the registry).

wow64.description: A 32-bit process on 64-bit Windows: its address space is measured.

addressLimit.description: With wow64: 2 GB, or 4 GB for a large-address-aware exe; reserved + committed bytes; the largest free block.

messages.name: netdbg.setEventTrace
messages.description: Traces the firing of event handlers without stopping: the engine reads the sender at each handler's entry and sends `netdbg.controlEvent`.

handlers.description: The handlers to trace (added to those already traced).

messages.name: netdbg.setValueWatches
messages.description: Break on Value Change: the names to watch and the lines that write them (the relay finds those in the workspace's C#, which the engine does not have). Replaces the earlier watches. At a write the engine reads the value, steps over the line and reads it again: when it changed it stops with reason `data breakpoint` (`text`: `name: old → new`), otherwise it goes on as if nothing happened. The write-site breakpoints are not reported to the client.

watches.description: Each name with its write sites (paths as the PDB has them; the relay maps them through `sourceFileMap`).
Per name: whether a site could be bound now (sites in modules not loaded yet bind when they load), and how many sites.

messages.name: netdbg.setExceptionTypes
messages.description: The exception types checked in the Exception Settings view changed: the relay stops on these when they are thrown.

messages.name: netdbg.changesApplied
messages.description: The result of applying code changes (Edit and Continue), whether VS Code asked (`netdbg.applyChanges`) or an AI client did through MCP (`debug_apply_changes`). The body is the response of `netdbg.applyChanges`.

messages.name: netdbg.controlEvent
messages.description: A traced event handler ran (event trace).

messages.name: netdbg.coverageChanged
messages.description: Lines were counted (at most 4 times a second): the rates as in `netdbg.coverage`, and the source files whose marks changed (read their lines with `netdbg.coverage { file }`).

messages.name: netdbg.exceptionThrown
messages.description: An exception was thrown (exception log): sent for every throw while the log is on, whether the program stops or not.

stopped.description: Whether the program stopped for it.

snapshot.description: Call stack and local variables at the throw (when exceptionLog.captureLocals is on).

messages.name: netdbg.mcpEndpoint
messages.description: Sent once after `initialize` when the engine was started with `--mcp-listen` (setting `netdbg.mcp.enabled`): where AI clients can control this session through MCP (Streamable HTTP, JSON answers only). The extension offers it to VS Code's AI as an HTTP MCP server. The engine also writes it to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\netdbg\mcp\<enginePid>.json` (removed on exit), where `netdbg --mcp-connect` finds it for AI clients outside VS Code.

url.description: `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`. Requests from a web page (an `Origin` other than localhost or VS Code) are refused.

token.description: Required as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; made anew for every engine.

messages.name: netdbg.removeBreakpoint
messages.description: A temporary (`#once`) breakpoint was hit: the extension removes it from VS Code's list.

messages.name: netdbg.sqlExecuted
messages.description: A statement read from a database command (SQL log), with its parameters and the frames that ran it.

method.description: The provider method that ran it (`System.Data.SqlClient.SqlCommand.ExecuteReader`).

messages.name: netdbg.trackedValues
messages.description: Values of a `#track:` logpoint hit, or the time of a `#timer-start:` / `#timer-end:` section.

messages.name: netdbg.uiFrozen
messages.description: A UI thread stopped answering window messages for `ms` while the program ran (launch argument `uiFreeze`): the engine pauses the program next, on that thread. The relay words the stop's reason in the user's language.

messages.name: output
messages.description: Standard DAP `output`. Categories: `stdout` / `stderr` (the program's output, decoded as UTF-8 while it is valid, else in the console code page), `console` (Debug.WriteLine and the engine's notes), `important` (an evaluation that had to run the other threads to finish).

messages.name: process
messages.description: Sent once the program is started or attached to (after the `configurationDone` response). The extension starts the memory graph and the UI freeze watch with `systemProcessId`.

name.description: The program's path (launch) or the process's exe (attach; for a crash dump, the exe in the dump).

systemProcessId.description: Absent for a crash dump (its process is not on this machine any more).

dumpProcessId.description: For a crash dump: the process number written in the dump.

messages.name: stopped
messages.description: Standard DAP `stopped`. The engine sends `breakpoint` (also function breakpoints), `step` (also arriving in a Step Into Target), `exception`, `pause` (also `Debugger.Break()` and a UI freeze, with `description`), `entry` and `data breakpoint` (Break on Value Change, with `description` / `text`); the relay sends `goto`.

ExpressionEvaluationOptions.description: The same option as the C# extension's debugger (vsdbg).

allowImplicitFuncEval.description: Run property getters and `ToString()` / `DebuggerDisplay` to show values (default true). When false, properties come with `presentationHint.lazy` and run only when expanded; explicit evaluations (watch, hover, console) still run code.

name.description: Type name as the Variables view shows it (`System.Collections.Generic.List<int>`).

standardRequests.notes: Answers with the capabilities below, then sends `initialized`. Reads `supportsInvalidatedEvent`.
Checks the program (exists, bitness of the engine, .NET Framework 4.x) and remembers it; starts it at `configurationDone`.
Checks the process (runtime loaded, bitness of the engine); attaches at `configurationDone`.
Starts or attaches, then sends `process`.

`condition` is a C# expression evaluated in the stopped program, or a marker (`#once`, `#after File.cs:12`, `#changed expr`, `#caller A, B`). The engine also judges `hitCondition` (`N`, `==N`, `>=N`, `>N`, `%N`) and `logMessage` (`{expr}`, `$FUNCTION`, `$TID`, `#track:`, `#timer-start:` / `#timer-end:`). The relay maps paths.
`Type.Method`, `Method`, `Namespace.Type.Method` (all overloads). `anyCode: true` binds outside user code too.
Filters `all` and `user-unhandled`; `filterOptions[].condition` is `A, B` or `!A, B` (type names).
`exceptionId` is `CLR/<type>`, `breakMode` `always` / `unhandled` / `userUnhandled`, `details` with `message`, `stackTrace`, `innerException`.
The OS thread id is the DAP thread id. Names are `Thread.Name`; else the process's first thread is `Main Thread` (listed first) and the others `<No name>`.

Every managed frame, named `Namespace.Type.Method()` with the real type arguments; `startFrame` / `levels` page them. A frame in an assembly without symbols points at its decompiled file (see `netdbg.decompile`).
One scope, `Locals`. A step over a call puts `<Type.Method> returned` first.
See the value conventions. Children carry `evaluateName`. `Static members` and `Raw View` are nodes of their own.
C# expressions with the compiler's values and types (lambdas, LINQ, `await` waited synchronously, pointers). The relay rewrites `$N` object ids.
The value is a C# expression.
Assigns to any assignable expression.
Frozen threads stay suspended.
Steps over `await` to the same method's continuation.
With `targetId`, steps into the chosen call (Step Into Specific): the engine steps over the line with a breakpoint on the target.
From an async method, returns to the awaiting caller.
The calls of the current statement, read from the IL, in the order they run (`Type.Method`, properties `Type.Name.get`).
Stops every thread (reason `pause`).
The lines of the same method that can be the next statement.
The engine moves the instruction pointer; the relay sends the `stopped` (reason `goto`).
Break on Value Change for a plain name. `setDataBreakpoints` finds the lines that write it in the workspace and sends them as `netdbg.setValueWatches`.
Cancels a running evaluation.
Ends the program; `exited` and `terminated` follow.
Ends a launched program, detaches from an attached one (`terminateDebuggee` overrides).

startup.name: --interpreter=vscode
startup.notes: DAP over stdin / stdout (the default; accepted for netcoredbg compatibility).

startup.name: --log=<file>
startup.notes: Writes the DAP traffic and the engine's own log, flushed per line (setting `netdbg.trace`).

startup.name: --mcp-listen
startup.notes: Also accepts MCP on 127.0.0.1 with a token, and sends `netdbg.mcpEndpoint` (setting `netdbg.mcp.enabled`). The tools drive this session; VS Code follows through the usual DAP events.

startup.name: --mcp-connect[=<enginePid>]
startup.notes: Not used by the extension: run by AI clients outside VS Code, a stdio MCP server that relays to the latest engine started with `--mcp-listen` (or the given one).

startup.name: NETCOREDBG_SYMBOL_DIRS
startup.notes: Environment variable: folders (separated by `;`) searched first for PDBs, by module MVID (downloaded symbols).

valueConventions.rule: `{Namespace.Type}`, or the `DebuggerDisplay` text; `DateTime`, `TimeSpan`, `Guid` and the like as `{ToString()}`.
Strings as C# literals (`"a\"b"`); chars as the code and the literal (`120 'x'`).
`{int[3]}`; collections with a DebuggerDisplay show it (`Count = 3`).
A value with an id ends with ` {$N}`; in expressions `$N` is sent as `__NETDBG_OBJID_N`.
Member names (`Read, Write` for flags); unnamed values as the number in the underlying type (`-6`).
The pointed value, with the pointer type in `type` (`int*`); `null` for 0.
The result is the exception object (`{System.InvalidOperationException}`); errors fail the request with a message saying what to do.
`Expression has been evaluated and has no value` with type `void`.
